prompt: Why can a bucket policy not hide the `phone` column of `part-0.csv` from the analysts?
hint: What is the smallest thing S3 hands out?

choices.text: Bucket policies cannot name a prefix, only a whole bucket
choices.why: They can; `curated/orders/*` is a perfectly good resource. The trouble is below the prefix.

choices.text: The column is inside the object, and S3 grants whole objects
choices.why: Right. `aws s3 cp` returned all four columns, because the object is the unit S3 knows.

choices.text: S3 hides columns for Parquet files and reads CSV files whole
choices.why: S3 knows nothing of the format; a Parquet file is an object like any other.

choices.text: The phone column is encrypted under a KMS key of its own
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson encrypts one column; the file is plain CSV.

prompt: With IAM alone and no Lake Formation, what must an analyst's role be allowed so that Athena can query a table? Choose all that apply.
hint: Two services, which know nothing of each other.

choices.text: `glue:GetTable` on the database and the table
choices.why: Yes. Without it Athena cannot find out what the table is.

choices.text: `s3:GetObject` on the table's prefix
choices.why: Yes. Without it the query fails on the first file.

choices.text: `lakeformation:GetDataAccess`
choices.why: That belongs to the path through Lake Formation, where the S3 permission is the one that goes away.

choices.text: `s3:PutObject` on the table's prefix
choices.why: Reading needs no write permission; that is for the pipeline that writes the files.

prompt: With IAM alone, what is the usual workaround for keeping one column away from a team?
hint: Nothing in IAM can hide a column.

choices.text: A `Deny` on the column, written in the bucket policy
choices.why: A bucket policy names buckets and keys; there is no column to deny.

choices.text: A list of the allowed columns in the role's IAM policy
choices.why: IAM has no condition that reaches inside an object.

choices.text: A second copy of the table, minus the column
choices.why: Right, and a second copy is a second thing to keep in step, pay for and protect.

choices.text: Renaming the column so the team cannot guess it
choices.why: A renamed column is still in the file, and the file is still read whole.

prompt: What does registering `s3://quitanda-curated-prod/curated` with Lake Formation do?
hint: Think about the credentials an engine is handed.

choices.text: It copies the files into Lake Formation's own storage
choices.why: Nothing moves and nothing is copied; the files stay in the bucket.

choices.text: It creates a Glue table for every prefix under the path
choices.why: That is a crawler's work, in lesson 16; this lesson wrote its table by hand.

choices.text: It lets Lake Formation vend credentials for the path
choices.why: Right. With `--use-service-linked-role` that role is one AWS creates for the purpose.

choices.text: It makes the path readable to anybody holding a grant, directly through S3
choices.why: S3 does not consult Lake Formation; grants are checked by the engines that ask.

prompt: After `put-data-lake-settings` was sent with only `DataLakeAdmins`, what had happened to the two default grants to `IAM_ALLOWED_PRINCIPALS`?
hint: Compare the two `get-data-lake-settings` answers.

choices.text: They were kept, because the call merges into the settings
choices.why: The second answer has no default grants at all; the call does not merge.

choices.text: They passed to the new administrator
choices.why: The administrator can grant anything, and holds no copy of the defaults.

choices.text: They became column grants on every table
choices.why: Nothing was converted; they were simply not in the new document.

choices.text: They were gone: the call replaces the whole document
choices.why: Right. On AWS, leaving them out is how new tables stop being handed to IAM.

prompt: The analyst holds `SELECT` on `order_id`, `customer_id`, `total_cents` and `dt`, and nothing else. On AWS, what does `SELECT * FROM curated.orders` return in Athena?
hint: Athena removes what the grant does not cover.

choices.text: Every column, since `*` is not a column name
choices.why: The grant is applied to what is returned, whatever the query spells.

choices.text: The four granted columns, without `phone`
choices.why: Right. A query that names `phone` is refused, and `*` returns the rest.

choices.text: Only `order_id`, the first column of the grant
choices.why: All four granted columns are readable; their order in the grant does not matter.

choices.text: An error, because `*` includes a column the analyst may not read
choices.why: Naming `phone` explicitly is refused; `*` is narrowed to the granted columns.

prompt: Put the steps of an Athena query on a Lake Formation table in order.
hint: The engine asks before it reads.
items: The analyst sends the query to Athena
Athena asks Lake Formation for access to the table, as the analyst
Lake Formation checks the grants and returns temporary credentials
Athena reads the files from S3 with those credentials
Athena returns only the granted columns to the analyst

prompt: In moto, every grant of this lesson succeeded and `get-temporary-glue-table-credentials` answered 404. What does that tell you about what the analyst could read on AWS?
hint: Who, in this lab, ever asks Lake Formation anything?

choices.text: That the analyst would be refused, since no credentials can be vended
choices.why: The 404 is a call moto does not implement, not a refusal AWS would give.

choices.text: That the analyst could read everything, since nothing was enforced
choices.why: Nothing was enforced because nothing asked; that says nothing about AWS.

choices.text: Nothing either way: moto stores the grants, and nothing asks it
choices.why: Right. A success from moto means the request was well formed.

choices.text: That the grants are correct, since moto accepted all of them
choices.why: moto accepted a grant on a table that does not exist, too.

prompt: Lake Formation is on. `orders` carries the analysts' column grant and also the default `ALL` to `IAM_ALLOWED_PRINCIPALS`. The analysts' IAM policy allows Athena, the catalogue and the bucket. On AWS, what do they read?
hint: What does that group mean?

choices.text: The four granted columns, as the column grant says
choices.why: With `IAM_ALLOWED_PRINCIPALS` holding `ALL`, IAM decides, and IAM allows every column.

choices.text: All five of them, since IAM is left to decide
choices.why: Right. The column grant is not in force until that grant is revoked.

choices.text: Nothing, because the two grants contradict each other
choices.why: Grants add up; they do not cancel.

choices.text: Only the columns tagged `internal`
choices.why: No tag-based grant was given to the analysts.

prompt: Which order of steps takes `orders` over to Lake Formation without breaking a query on the way?
hint: Between the two steps, which door is open?

choices.text: Revoke `IAM_ALLOWED_PRINCIPALS` on the table, then grant its users in Lake Formation
choices.why: Between the two, IAM's door has closed and Lake Formation's has not opened, so every query fails.

choices.text: Grant its users in Lake Formation, then revoke `IAM_ALLOWED_PRINCIPALS` on the table
choices.why: Right. The new door is open before the old one closes.

choices.text: Deregister the location, then grant its users
choices.why: Without a registered location Lake Formation cannot vend credentials for the table at all.

choices.text: Remove the users' IAM policies, then revoke `IAM_ALLOWED_PRINCIPALS`
choices.why: They still need Athena and the catalogue in IAM; it is the S3 permission that goes.

prompt: Every Lake Formation grant on `orders` is right and `IAM_ALLOWED_PRINCIPALS` has been revoked, but a script's role still has `s3:GetObject` on `quitanda-curated-prod/curated/*`. What can the script read?
hint: Which service does `aws s3 cp` talk to?

choices.text: Only the columns it holds grants on, since the location is registered
choices.why: Registration lets Lake Formation vend credentials; S3 still answers its own permissions.

choices.text: Nothing, since a registered location refuses direct reads
choices.why: S3 has never heard of Lake Formation; a direct read is judged by IAM and the bucket policy.

choices.text: Every column, with `aws s3 cp`: S3 never consults Lake Formation
choices.why: Right. The second half of taking over a lake is removing that permission.

choices.text: Only the files of the tables it holds `SELECT` on
choices.why: S3 knows nothing of tables or of `SELECT`.

prompt: In ___ access mode, a registered location keeps answering IAM's permissions for everybody, while the principals opted in one by one are judged by Lake Formation's grants.
hint: It is the gentle way to move a lake many teams use.

prompt: `orders` is tagged `sensitivity=internal`, and its `phone` column `sensitivity=pii`. An analyst is granted `SELECT` on the expression `sensitivity=internal`. On AWS, what can the analyst read?
hint: A column can override the tag it inherits.

choices.text: Every column, since the table is `internal`
choices.why: `phone` was given its own value for the same key, so it is not `internal`.

choices.text: Only `phone`
choices.why: That is the one column the expression does not match.

choices.text: Nothing, since a column needs a grant of its own
choices.why: A tag-based grant covers every resource whose tags match, columns included.

choices.text: Every column of `orders` except `phone`
choices.why: Right. The table's tag flows down to four columns, and `phone` carries `pii`.

prompt: Next week the pipeline creates a table and tags it `sensitivity=internal`. What has to be done before the support role can read it?
hint: Support was granted an expression, not a table.

choices.text: Nothing: the existing tag grant covers it
choices.why: Right. That is the point of tags, and also why tagging is a sensitive permission.

choices.text: A grant on the new table for the support role
choices.why: That would be the per-table grant that tags exist to replace.

choices.text: Running the tag-based grant again
choices.why: The expression is evaluated against the tags as they are; it does not need repeating.

choices.text: Registering the table's location again
choices.why: A location is registered once, for every table under it.

prompt: Why is the permission to assign LF-tags as sensitive as the data itself?
hint: Grants follow the tags.

choices.text: Every tag assignment is billed
choices.why: The price sheet has no line for Lake Formation permissions at all.

choices.text: A tag, once assigned, can never be changed
choices.why: Tags can be changed, as `phone` overriding its table's value showed; that is the danger, not the safety.

choices.text: Tags are written into the S3 objects and travel with copies
choices.why: LF-tags live in the catalogue, not in the files.

choices.text: Whoever tags a table decides which tag grants cover it, and so who reads it
choices.why: Right. Tagging a table `pii` by mistake hands it to support on the spot.

prompt: On AWS, `support-filter.json` applied to the three rows of `part-0.csv` lets support see some rows and some columns. How many cells, rows times columns, does it let through?
hint: Count the customers in the row filter and the names in `ColumnNames`.

prompt: Which command lists every Lake Formation grant for an audit?
hint: It was run with `--output table`.

choices.text: `aws iam list-policies`
choices.why: Those are IAM policies; Lake Formation grants are not among them.

choices.text: `aws glue get-tables`
choices.why: That lists the tables, not who may read them.

choices.text: `aws lakeformation list-permissions`
choices.why: Right. With no filter it is every grant, and a `--query` makes it readable.

choices.text: `aws s3api get-bucket-policy`
choices.why: The bucket policy is the S3 side; it holds no table or column grant.

prompt: moto accepted a grant on `ordres`, a table that does not exist, and Glue says it is not there. What does that show?
hint: Did anything compare the grant with the catalogue?

choices.text: Lake Formation creates a table at its first grant
choices.why: Glue still answers that `ordres` is not found.

choices.text: moto stores grants and checks none against the catalogue
choices.why: Right. moto enforces none of Lake Formation.

choices.text: Lake Formation and Glue use separate catalogues on AWS
choices.why: Lake Formation grants on the Glue Data Catalog itself.

choices.text: The grant is reserved for when somebody creates `ordres`, by design
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson describes reserved grants; it is a typing mistake that was stored.

prompt: Which of these belong on the defender's list? Choose all that apply.
hint: Each one closes a door the lesson showed open.

choices.text: Grant to roles rather than to individual users
choices.why: Yes. People come and go without grants left behind.

choices.text: Take direct S3 access away from principals that read through an engine
choices.why: Yes. Otherwise `aws s3 cp` reads every column.

choices.text: Alert on `GrantPermissions` for the `pii` tag
choices.why: Yes. A new reader of phone numbers is noticed the day it appears.

choices.text: Keep `IAM_ALLOWED_PRINCIPALS` on sensitive tables as a fallback
choices.why: While it holds `ALL`, the column grants on that table are not in force.

choices.text: Give every analyst the permission to assign tags
choices.why: Whoever tags decides who reads; that permission is granted as carefully as the data.

prompt: Match each symptom to its cause.
hint: Each one is a door the lesson named.

pairs.left: Analysts see `phone` despite their column grant
Every query on a table fails after a change
pairs.right: IAM's grant was revoked before any Lake Formation grant existed

pairs.left: Support cannot read a new table
pairs.right: It carries no tag that support's expression matches

pairs.left: A script reads every column with `aws s3 cp`
pairs.right: Its role keeps `s3:GetObject` on the registered location

right_distractors: Athena scanned more bytes than the query needed

prompt: Quitanda wants each district's support team to see phone numbers only for that district's customers. Which Lake Formation feature does that?
hint: Some rows and some columns at once.

choices.text: An LF-tag `pii` on the `phone` column, granted to each team
choices.why: A tag covers the whole column, for every row.

choices.text: A data filter on rows and columns, granted to each team
choices.why: Right. Rows and columns together are cells, and the filter is what narrows a grant to them.

choices.text: A column grant on `phone` for every support role
choices.why: That shows `phone` for every customer, not one district's.

choices.text: A bucket policy on each district's prefix in the curated bucket
choices.why: The files are partitioned by day, not by district, and S3 grants whole files.

prompt: Which of these calls failed with a 404 in moto, so that the lesson could not run it?
hint: One kind of permission was described entirely from the documentation.

choices.text: `register-resource`
choices.why: It succeeded, and `list-resources` showed the location.

choices.text: `create-lf-tag`
choices.why: It succeeded; the tag was then added to the table and a column.

choices.text: `grant-permissions` on an `LFTagPolicy`
choices.why: It succeeded and appeared in `list-permissions`.

choices.text: `create-data-cells-filter`
choices.why: Right. Row and cell filtering were taught from AWS's documentation.
